summary: Arthur William Ryder was an Indologist. He earned his A.B. at Harvard and Ph.D. at Leipzig, also studying at Berlin and under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He was an instructor at Harvard (1902–1906) and Sanskrit professor at UC Berkeley (~1906–1938).
Arthur Woollgar Verrall studied at Wellington College (~1865–1870) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1870–1874). He taught Robert Alexander Neil.
Aruna Haldar worked in Indology and philosophy. She studied under Kedarnath Ojha and Girindrasekhar Bose, and served as a teacher at Patna University.

Arunoday Natvarlal Jani was an Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. at Mumbai under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt and studied under M. V. Upadhyay. At Baroda, he was a Sanskrit lecturer and professor (1967–1980), later directing the Oriental Institute (1975–1981).

Arvind Sharma works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Allahabad, Syracuse, and Harvard. He held posts at the University of Queensland (1976–1980), University of Sydney (1980), Harvard, and McGill University (Birks Chair in Comparative Religion, 1994).

Asanga Tilakaratne works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. At the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, he served as Head of Buddhist Thought (attested 1993), Professor (~2003–2006), and Professor and Head of Buddhist Philosophy at the University of Kelaniya.
Asatoshi Kamiya studied Buddhist studies as a graduate student at Komazawa University (attested 1973). He later worked as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School (attested 1978).

Asen Balikci earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1956. He worked at the Canadian Museum of History (1954), National Museum of Canada (~1957–1968), and was Professor of Ethnology at the Université de Montréal (1963–1993).

Ashok Aklujkar is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Pune University and completed his Ph.D. at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served in the Department of Asian Studies at the University of British Columbia (1969–2006).

Ashok Gangadean is a philosopher who completed his PhD at Brandeis University. In 1981, he was appointed Margaret Gest Professor of Global Philosophy at Haverford College, and he founded the Global Dialogue Institute.

Ashok Kumar Chatterjee studied philosophy at Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti, earning his BA, MA, and PhD. He was a professor and department head at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University (1950–1963) and Banaras Hindu University (1963–1985).

Ashok Kumar Malhotra is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the East-West Center (~1964–1969) and founded the Yoga and Meditation Society for the Scientific Study of Spirituality.

Ashutosh Mukherjee studied at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta. He served on the Calcutta High Court (1904), was Tagore Professor of Law (1906–1914) and later post-holder (1921–1923) at Calcutta University, and presided over The Asiatic Society (~1907–1915).

Asim Kumar Chatterjee is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his Ph.D. under D. Mukherjee at the University of Calcutta by 1967, where he was a Senior Research Fellow (attested 1970). He also lectured at Jangipur College.

Asko Parpola is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pentti Aalto, R. Panneerselvam, and P. R. Subramanian. He held positions at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies (1968), Academy of Finland, and served as Professor at the University of Helsinki (~1982–2004).

Astley John Hilary Goodwin was a history and archaeology scholar. He studied at St. John's College, Johannesburg, Selwyn College, and SOAS University of London. He took up a post at the University of Cape Town in 1923.

Atsuhiko Yoshida studied at Seikei University, University of Tokyo, and under Georges Dumézil. He held research and teaching posts at CNRS (~1961–1969), Seikei University (professor, 1970), and Gakushuin University (professor, 2006).
Atsushi Ibuki studied at Waseda University and works in Buddhist studies. He held a post as professor at Toyo University (attested 2015).

Atsushi Kanazawa is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He was a lecturer at the Meteorological College (attested 1986–1989) and an assistant professor and faculty member at Komazawa University (~1996–~2004).
Atsushi Kiyozawa completed his doctoral coursework at the University of Delhi in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Kindai University (attested 1989).
